Report_ID: Score on the knowledge questionnaire (0–10) at 1 month
Title: Using an informed consent in mammography screening: a randomized trial
Author: Baena-Cañada JM, Rosado-Varela P, Expósito-Álvarez I, González-Guerrero M, Nieto-Vera J, Benítez-Rodríguez E
Comment: M_diff computed as intervention mean minus control mean (3.95 − 3.43) from explicitly reported means in a simple two-arm between-subjects design; not reported by the paper. df1=353 inferred as n1+n2−2 (independent t-test); the t statistic itself was not reported. Ns are the numbers analysed for knowledge (178 control, 177 intervention), which differ from the randomized Ns shown in Table 1 column headers (218/216).
domain: breast cancer screening / informed decision making
Study Environment: Screening program centre (in-person first interview) with 1-month telephone follow-up
Medium: verbal explanation plus printed leaflet (Nordic Cochrane Centre document)
Topic of Content: Benefits and risks of mammography screening (mortality benefit, overdiagnosis/overtreatment, false positives, radiation, breast pain, false reassurance)
Participant type: Women aged 45–67 attending population-based mammography breast cancer screening
Recruitment source: Cadiz-La Janda Health District breast cancer screening program, Cádiz, Spain (recruited at the Program Centre after mammography, January 2011–September 2012)

Outcome variable: Score on the knowledge questionnaire (0–10) at 1 month

Report_ID: Objective knowledge score about benefits and risks of mammography screening
Title: Willingness to Participate in Mammography Screening: A Randomized Controlled Questionnaire Study of Responses to Two Patient Information Leaflets With Different Factual Content
Author: Gummersbach E, in der Schmitten J, Mortsiefer A, Abholz HH, Wegscheider K, Pentzek M
Comment: M_diff computed as group_2_mean - group_1_mean (5.23 - 5.49 = -0.26) per the extraction formula; note the paper's own framing is that the new (intervention) leaflet scored 0.26 points HIGHER, so the intervention-favouring difference is +0.26. Knowledge n per arm (161/168) is lower than the analysed N per arm (178/175) because of missing items. Methods/eTable 1 state the score ranges 0-10, while the Results text says 'scale of 1 to 10'. Group difference was tested with a Mann-Whitney U test although means and SDs are reported. Participants were recruited from 33 family practices but the authors explicitly did not expect and did not model a cluster effect; no ICC reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Group A - new (2010 onward) more informative mammography screening leaflet') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomized controlled trial (blinded, parallel-group questionnaire study)
domain: breast cancer screening / shared decision making
Medium: printed patient information leaflet mailed with a postal questionnaire
Topic of Content: benefits and harms of mammography screening (false positives, overdiagnosis, mortality reduction, interval cancers)
Participant type: women aged 48-49 years, not yet invited to mammography screening, recruited from 33 family practices
Recruitment source: 33 family practices in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany (patient lists)
Outcome measurement: Mean objective knowledge score (points, 0-10 scale) per leaflet group, with 95% CI and SD; compared with Mann-Whitney U test
Outcome variable: Objective knowledge score about benefits and risks of mammography screening
outcome_units: points on a 0-10 objective knowledge score

Title: Effects of a leaflet on breast cancer screening knowledge, explicit attitudes, and implicit associations
Author: Kregting et al.
Comment: No SD, SE or confidence interval is reported for the knowledge means; Table 2 reports mean with observed RANGE (leaflet 4-11, control 2-11), which is NOT a measure of dispersion usable as SD. The p-value is only given as "<0.001" (recorded here as 0.001, an upper bound), so an exact SD cannot be validly derived from the p-value either. Ranges were entered in the *_range_* fields only to document what the paper reports; the paper's central values are MEANS, not medians. M_diff not computed to avoid sign ambiguity (the paper lists the leaflet arm first); both means are explicit (9.9 leaflet vs 9.6 control). Ns are the numbers analysed at follow-up per arm.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Leaflet condition (official RIVM breast cancer screening information leaflet)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
domain: breast cancer screening / informed choice communication
Topic of Content: benefits and harms of breast cancer screening, including overdiagnosis, overtreatment, false-negatives and interval cancers
Participant type: Women aged 49-75 eligible for and invited to the Dutch breast cancer screening programme
Recruitment source: Regional screening organisation 'Bevolkingsonderzoek Zuid-West', South West screening region, the Netherlands
Outcome measurement: Mean number of correct answers out of 11 statements on screening process, outcomes, benefits and harms

Author: Pérez-Lacasta MJ, Martínez-Alonso M, Garcia M, Sala M, Perestelo-Pérez L, Vidal C, et al.
Comment: No SDs are reported for the knowledge scores in Table 3; only the mean difference with a cluster-adjusted (Rao-Scott) 95% CI is given. SE_diff = (6.44 − 4.50)/3.92 = 0.4949 was DERIVED from the reported 95% CI; group SDs were not reported and are left empty. p-value reported only as "<0.001" (entered as 0.001). Cluster-randomised design (40 Basic Health Areas, ~10 women per cluster; ICC assumed 0.1 in the sample-size calculation) — the reported CI is already cluster-adjusted, so no further design-effect deflation was applied to the Ns recorded here.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention: decision aid leaflet with detailed information on benefits and harms of breast screening') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type

Report_ID: Total knowledge score across all subscales (conceptual + numerical; 22 marks available)
Title: Use of a decision aid including information on overdetection to support informed choice about breast cancer screening: a randomised controlled trial
Author: Hersch J, Barratt A, Jansen J, Irwig L, McGeechan K, Jacklyn G, Thornton H, Dhillon H, Houssami N, McCaffery K
Comment: No SDs are reported for knowledge scores in Table 3. M_diff (1.66) is the paper's OWN reported difference (intervention minus control, i.e. group_1 minus group_2), not computed as group_2 - group_1; sign is positive favouring the intervention. SE_diff was DERIVED from the reported 95% CI as (2.21 - 1.11)/3.92 = 0.281; per-arm SDs could be derived downstream as SD ≈ sqrt(n) x CI width / 3.92 but are not reported verbatim. p value reported as "<0.0001" and entered as 0.0001. Both arms received an information booklet (active comparator: identical booklet with overdetection content omitted) plus the standard NSW screening programme leaflet; neither arm included a values-clarification exercise. Ns are the numbers completing follow-up (419 per arm) as given in the Table 3 column headers.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention decision aid (overdetection information included) + standard NSW screening leaflet') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: randomised controlled trial, parallel-group, individually randomised
domain: breast cancer screening / shared decision making
Medium: printed decision aid booklet mailed to participants; outcomes by telephone interview
Topic of Content: Benefits and harms of mammography screening (breast cancer mortality reduction, false positives, overdetection)
Participant type: Community-dwelling women aged 48-50 years without mammography in the past 2 years and without personal or strong family history of breast cancer
Recruitment source: Random cohort of women aged 48-50 years extracted from the NSW Electoral Commission electoral register; recruited by telephone
Outcome measurement: Mean total knowledge score (marks out of 22) per arm, with mean difference and 95% CI; two-sample t test
Outcome variable: Total knowledge score across all subscales (conceptual + numerical; 22 marks available)
